newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tatneft Eurobond won't happen before H2.
newsitem.headline: Tatneft Eurobond won't happen before H2.

text.p: Russian oil company Tatneft will issue a Eurobond no earlier than the second half of the year, foreign economic director Eduard Akopdzhanov said.
"It is too early to talk about volumes and conditions -- the issue prospectus has not even been approved yet," he said.

Tatneft, based in the eastern European Russian republic of Tatarstan, sent the prospectus to the republic government for approval on February 15, Konstantin Kolesnik, head of the securities division of the Tatarstan Ministry of Finance, said.
Kolesnik also said that before approval of the Eurobond Tatneft would have to present 1996 results, currently being audited by Price Waterhouse.
Tatneft plans its annual shareholders meeting for June but has not set a date, a spokesman said, adding that preliminary 1996 financial results could be ready by mid-April.
Foreign investors own 11.6 percent of Tatneft.
